title: The Race Around the Park: Speed and Velocity

pages.text: The Race Around the Park A Story About Speed and Velocity Emma and Noah visited a large neighborhood park with their family on a Saturday morning. The park had a running path that went all the way around a beautiful lake. Dad smiled. "Who wants to race to the big oak tree?" "I do!" Emma shouted. "So do I!" Noah laughed. Both children started running. Emma ran very fast. Noah ran a little slower. When they reached the tree, Dad smiled. "You both moved quickly." "But today we're going to learn the difference between speed and velocity."

How Fast Did We Go? Dad looked at his stopwatch. "Emma ran 100 meters in 20 seconds." "How fast was I?" Emma asked. Dad smiled. "Speed tells us how fast something moves." It only uses two things: distance traveled and time taken. "So speed doesn't care which way we ran?" Emma asked. "Exactly!" Dad replied. "It only cares how much distance you covered." Speed tells us how fast something moves, but it does not tell us the direction. Speed formula: Speed equals distance divided by time.

Going Somewhere Dad pointed farther down the trail. "Now let's try something different," he said. He asked the children to run straight to the playground. When they arrived, Dad asked, "Did you notice something?" "This time," he explained, "I didn't just care about how fast you ran. I also cared where you ended up." "When speed also tells us the direction of motion, we call it velocity." Emma smiled. "So velocity is speed with direction!" "Exactly!" Dad replied. Speed tells us how fast. Velocity tells us how fast and in which direction.

A Funny Walk Dad drew a circle on the walking path. "Walk one complete lap around the lake." The children did as he said. When they returned to the exact place where they had started, Dad asked, "How far did you walk?" "One whole lap!" Noah answered. "Correct. But where did you end up?" "Right where we started." Dad nodded. "So your distance was one whole lap. But your displacement was zero. Velocity depends on displacement, not just distance." Distance is the total path traveled. Displacement is the straight-line change from start to finish and includes direction. You can walk a long distance, but if you end up where you started, your displacement is zero.

Two Friends, Same Speed Soon, two cyclists came along the path. "One is going north at 10 km per hour," said Dad. "The other is going south at 10 km per hour." "They have the same speed!" Emma laughed. "They do," Dad said. "But their velocities are different because they are moving in opposite directions." "So speed tells us how fast. Velocity tells us how fast and which direction." "Now I understand!" Noah said. "Me too!" Emma smiled. Same speed, different direction means different velocities.

Science Element Speed tells us how fast something moves. It depends on distance traveled and time taken. Speed equals distance divided by time. Velocity tells us how fast and in which direction something moves. It depends on displacement and time. Two cars can have the same speed but different velocities if they travel in different directions. Distance is the total path traveled with no direction. Displacement is the straight-line change from start to finish and includes direction; it can be zero. Everyday examples: car speedometers show speed, GPS navigation uses velocity because direction matters, athletes measure speed, and pilots use velocity to know how fast they are going and in which direction. Remember: Speed means how fast. Velocity means how fast plus direction. Distance is the total path traveled. Displacement is the shortest straight-line change from start to finish.
